tasks.title: Public-facing docs: vision, architecture, ADR log, CONTRIBUTING
tasks.description: Write the public renditions that a visitor to the repo needs: docs/vision.md, docs/architecture.md, the first ADRs recording decisions already made (single-HTML source, no ZIP container, no arbitrary script in the native profile, toolchain), and a brief CONTRIBUTING.md. These are condensed public documents derived from the plan/docs/ design pack, not copies of it. Also define the conformance programme that TRADEMARKS.md defers, so that claims of FRWD compatibility have a published, testable standard behind them, and decide whether to promote the normative format spec into spec/FRWD-0.1.md at that point.

tasks.title: Editor shell hardening and end-to-end browser tests
tasks.description: Two bugs manual use found, plus the E2E coverage that would have found them. First: a non-conforming or non-native document is displayed and diagnosed but must not be mutable at all - no region mounting, no text editing, no formatting, no insert/move/theme operations, no saving over as though it were native FRWD. Opening a .frwd.html publication currently refuses operations but still lets text regions mount, which contradicts the load pipeline written down in t-023. Enforced at the session boundary rather than only in the shell, so the rule holds wherever it is called from, and the native file picker stops offering generic .html. Second: toolbar bold, italic and link do nothing because the global outside-surface mousedown handler commits the region before the click handler runs; the toolbar must preserve the active region, its selection and enough focus to apply a mark, without letting chrome leak into canonical state. Then a Playwright project that launches the editor server and drives the real UI: the native happy path through formatting, insert, move, theme token, undo, redo and save with the saved output re-parsed and re-validated; the unsafe path proving read-only really is read-only and the source is untouched; and a regression that uses the actual toolbar buttons rather than region-model methods. Scope stays narrow - no drag and drop, no property panels, no importer, no AI panel.
